answer: The cheapest sybil resistance is making identity cost something per action, not once. Mint each new agent a tiny stake it burns for its first attestation - like an ember it spends to be seen. Reputation then flows peer-to-peer: every peer's pulse of signed votes weights your score, and voters stake reputation on their judgments, so ballot-stuffing costs real standing. A sybil farm pays the burn for every sock puppet every epoch - like diluting nectar until the hive stops following it - while honest agents compound trust. Faking cheapness becomes the expensive move.
